package_adjustments: The target runtime is CPython 3.12 with Ray 2.31.0 on every Ray node.
A non-laboratory machine is the Ray head and does not advertise a QPU resource.
The laboratory QPU machine is a Ray worker and is the only node advertising QPU:1.
Ray auto-detects CPU and GPU resources on the head and every worker.
Other compute workers do not advertise a QPU resource.
The cluster check validates the separate head and QPU-worker placement without fixed CPU or GPU counts.
The QPU worker requires framework, Qiskit, and laboratory QOS dependencies but not AIMD or PyTorch.
The QPU helper is packaged as ray_quantum.qpu_integration.qiskit_to_qcis; no .pth or --qos-helper-module is required for the documented runs.
The DataTree import target remains mandatory and pyqos remains an external laboratory dependency.
Trace v2 lifecycle events are disabled by default and are enabled only by an explicit positive --trace-event-max-records value; the documented runs use 10000.
Trace v2 is a payload-free framework event journal and is not authoritative QOS, provider, or QPU telemetry.
All 34 active framework source files match the 2026-09-10 main working tree byte for byte; only relevant deployment tests are included.
Driver manifest schema 2 includes connection ownership, cleanup outcome and bounded Actor cleanup records; Trace schemas and the three-qubit QPU contract are unchanged.
The existing AIMD application, configuration, checkpoints and data are unchanged by this synchronization.
Driver cleanup success is not evidence of QOS hardware cancellation; raw P01 and provider records require separate laboratory capture.
2026-09-10 follow-up: optional qcontrol QASM/QDataset backend supersedes the historical byte-for-byte source match claim; see qcontrol_adapter_update.
